QF.id: VI Public Offering and Corporate Actions_19

question.text: For bonus shares of unlisted companies, where are they credited?

answer.text: To the normal ISIN of the company
To a temporary ISIN frozen for debit
Bonus shares are not issued by unlisted companies

explanation.text: The Logic: In the case of unlisted companies, bonus shares are credited to the normal ISIN of the company. This differs from listed companies, where bonus shares are credited to a temporary ISIN frozen for debit until the shares are available for trading. The Trap: One might apply the listed company rule (temporary ISIN) to unlisted companies, but the process differs. Note: Per the Series VI workbook (p.188), listed-company bonus shares use a temporary ISIN frozen for debit until the shares are available for trading, while unlisted-company bonus shares are credited to the normal ISIN.
